Definition: a marsh; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds
BiblicalUsage: Agam is a pool or marsh — standing water, reeds and rushes. Moses stretches his rod over the waters of Egypt and the pools turn to blood; Isaiah says Babylon will become a possession for the bittern and pools of water; and the same prophet promises that the parched ground will become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water.
TheologicalSignificance: On its own this word carries little theological weight; the meaning that matters lives in the verse around it, not in the word itself; in this case, the verse is Exodus 7:19.
